date.noteEn: Henderson places the Qantir production evidence in this century. Rehren and Pusch assign its glass-bearing layers provisionally to early Ramesside activity, pending final stratigraphic interpretation. The endpoints do not establish a workshop's opening or closure, continuous production throughout the century, or the first manufacture of glass in Egypt.

events.titleEn: Glassmakers produce raw glass at Qantir
events.summaryEn: Workshops at Qantir make glass from raw materials and prepare coloured ingots. These stages are distinguished from the work of shaping finished objects in other workshops. The excavated production debris reveals specialized craft activity; the detailed reconstruction of its processes remains an archaeological interpretation.
events.selectionNote: A notable, site-specific production system evidenced by workshop debris, distinct from Egypt's earlier introduction of glass and the uncertain onset of local manufacture. It adds an attested later craft installation rather than an invention claim or an isolated luxury object. The century-wide archaeological placement does not turn into a century of uninterrupted production. The synthesis and excavation discussion share underlying research.
